threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, touchpoints, and overall pilot plan.

messages.text: Team, welcome to the official channel for the Cross-Channel Customer Feedback Improvement Pilot. The goal is to design and run a 6-week pilot to better capture and act on customer feedback. I've attached the initial project brief. Our first step is to finalize the scope. Let's start by confirming the customer touchpoints we'll include. I've started the process map in A1, based on my initial understanding. Please review and add anything I've missed from your areas.

Thanks for kicking this off. Looking at A1, the help desk touchpoints (phone, email, portal tickets) are covered. A key point for us will be ensuring any new process integrates with our existing ticketing system without major changes, as per the project constraints. We also need to be very clear on the data privacy side from the start.

Great initiative. For the insurance team, our primary feedback channels are formal complaint emails and calls logged against policies. These are currently handled in a separate system. We need to ensure the mapping process for these specific cases is robust. I've added a note to A1 about this. The 30-day deadline is tight but achievable if we scope correctly.
Hi everyone! For membership, we have our welcome calls and the annual renewal survey. Should we also include social media comments? We get a lot of feedback there.

Good question. Given the pilot's constraints on using existing tools and the complexity of social media APIs, let's keep social media out of scope for now. We can add it to the roadmap for a future phase. Let's focus on direct interaction channels: help desk tickets, insurance complaints, membership calls/surveys, and on-site visits.
Ok, that makes sense. I will focus on the calls and survey then.
Hello. For the cellar, we only get feedback in person during tours. We can't have anything that slows down the tour groups, especially during harvest season. A simple paper form would be best.
Absolutely, the process must be lightweight for your team. We'll design a simple checklist for on-site feedback. That's a key part of T1, mapping these different needs.

Okay, so to confirm the scope (D1): We are including Help Desk (phone/email/portal), Insurance (complaint logs), Membership (calls/surveys), and Cellar (in-person checklists). Social media is out of scope for this pilot. Does everyone agree?
Agreed.
Confirmed.
Yes, agree.
OK.

Great. Now for the timeline. The project brief states a 30-day deadline to complete the pilot run (T11) and deliver the final report. This means we need to have the process defined and tools configured in the next two weeks. Week 1: Finalize scope and taxonomy. Week 2: Finalize scripts and dashboard setup. Weeks 3-4: Run pilot, collect data. Week 5 (into the next month): Analyze and report. Does this high-level plan work for everyone?
The timeline is aggressive but feasible. The critical path for me is agreeing on the taxonomy so I can start mapping our existing complaint codes.
From an ICT standpoint, the main dependency is clarity on the routing rules before we can finalize any script logic. The timeline seems fine if we can make decisions quickly in week 1.
Sounds good to me.
Excellent. Let's lock in this 30-day timeline and the key milestones. (D2). I'll take the lead on T1 and share an updated version of A1 by EOD for final review.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise the unified feedback taxonomy and routing rules.

messages.text: Alright team, following our kickoff, here is the first draft of the Unified Feedback Taxonomy (A2). I've created about 15 categories based on common themes I've seen in past reports. Please review and provide feedback, especially on whether these categories make sense for your specific areas. This is the core of T2.

Thanks. I've reviewed A2. The general categories are a good start. For insurance, we need more granularity under 'Product Issues'. I suggest sub-tags for 'Claim Process', 'Policy Wording', and 'Pricing Query'. This is critical for T7, as it will allow us to map our internal codes accurately. I've added these as suggestions directly in the document.

This looks solid. From a help desk perspective, the 'Technical Issue' category should probably be split into 'Website Bug' and 'Account Access Problem'. This will help us route tickets internally much faster without manual review. Once we finalize the tags, we can define the logic for routing and logging them in A5.
Excellent suggestions, @225681 and @17689. I've incorporated those changes into A2. The added granularity is exactly what we need.
What about a category for 'Positive Feedback'? It would be nice to track when members say good things about us.
Good point, @29126. I had a general 'Compliment' category. Is that sufficient, or do you think we need something more specific for 'Positive Feedback'?
Oh I see it now. Yes, 'Compliment' works fine, sorry I missed that.
The list seems long. For the cellar visits, we can probably only use three or four of these. 'Visit Experience', 'Product Feedback', 'Staff Compliment', 'Safety Concern'. That's all we have time for.
That's perfectly fine, @37334. Each channel will only use the relevant categories. The full list in A2 is just the master taxonomy. We'll make sure the checklist for your team is short and simple.
Okay, with the latest changes, I think we have a final list of categories and tags. I'm marking this as the approved version in A2. (D3). Any final objections?
Looks good. I can proceed with T7 now.
No objections from me.

Perfect. Now for the routing rules (D4). Based on the taxonomy, I've drafted the routing logic in the 'Routing' tab of A5. The principle is: feedback is logged centrally, and the owner is assigned based on the primary tag. For example, 'Claim Process' routes to Insurance, 'Website Bug' to Help Desk. Please review the rules for your area.
Routing rules for insurance tags are correct. I approve.
Help desk routing looks correct. This is clear enough to build into our intake script.
Looks good for membership.
Cellar feedback will be passed to BI manually, so this is fine.
Excellent, we have consensus. D3 and D4 are now confirmed. This unblocks several other tasks. @225681, you can proceed with T7. @17689, you can now finalize the script for T3. Great work everyone.

threads.thread_goal: Align on frontline scripts, checklists, and training approach.

messages.text: Hi team, now that we have the taxonomy, I've drafted the Help Desk intake script for T3. You can find it in A4. It includes the standard greeting, a data privacy notice, and questions to guide the agent to the correct feedback category. I've tried to keep it conversational. Feedback is welcome.

Thanks! I've taken a look. It seems a bit formal. Maybe we can make the language friendlier? For example, instead of 'state the nature of your feedback', we could say 'how can I help you today?'. We want our members to feel welcome.

That's a fair point. The initial part is our standard greeting, but I can adjust the feedback-specific questions to be more open-ended. I'll update that. I can also create a similar version for the membership team's proactive calls as part of T4.

The script is well-structured. The data privacy notice is crucial. One small but important point: if the feedback is related to an insurance policy, the agent must verify the caller's identity with two data points before logging anything. This is a compliance requirement. We should add a conditional step for that.

Excellent catch, @225681. I completely agree. I'll add a branching path in the script: IF feedback tag is 'Insurance-*', THEN perform identity verification. I've updated A4 with this logic and the friendlier tone suggested by @29126.
This is great collaboration. The script in A4 looks much stronger now. Are we ready to sign off on this version for the pilot? (D5)
Approved from my side.
Yes, it's good now.

Great. D5 is confirmed. Now for the cellar. @37334, as discussed, we need a simple checklist for T6. I've created a draft in A3. It's a one-page document with checkboxes for the 4-5 relevant categories. Can you confirm if this format works and when your team would use it during tours?

I looked at A3. Yes, this is simple enough. We can use this at the end of the tour, during the final tasting. That is the only time we have a few minutes where people are stationary. It must be on a clipboard.
Perfect. We'll ensure they are printed and available on clipboards. So we confirm the checklist format in A3 and its use at the end of the tour. (D6).
Now that we have the scripts, what about training? I am responsible for T10. I can schedule a meeting with everyone.

Good thinking, @29126. Let's do a short, 30-minute session for each team rather than one big meeting. It will be more focused. You can coordinate with the team leads to find a time next week. Please prepare a brief training slide deck covering the new taxonomy and the scripts.
Ok, will do.

threads.thread_goal: Set up KPI tracking, data protection rules, and dashboard expectations.

messages.text: Team, let's finalize our measurement plan. For T5, I need to set up the pilot dashboard. I've listed three core KPIs to start: 1. Total Feedback Volume (by channel), 2. Feedback by Category (top 5), and 3. Average Time to Acknowledge. Do these feel right to evaluate the pilot's success?

Those are good baseline KPIs. I'd propose adding a fourth: 'Re-routing Rate'. This would measure how often a ticket is initially mis-categorized and needs to be reassigned. It's a direct indicator of how well the new taxonomy and scripts are working. We can track this by looking at the edit history of the 'owner' field in A5.
That's a fantastic suggestion, @225681. 'Re-routing Rate' is a great quality metric. I'll add it to the list. The data will come from A6, which will be a clean export from our log.
Can we also track the number of compliments we get?
Yes, the 'Feedback by Category' KPI will show that. 'Compliment' will be one of the categories we can filter on.
So, to confirm, our four core KPIs are: Volume, Category Mix, Time to Acknowledge, and Re-routing Rate. (D7). Everyone aligned?

Agreed. On a related note, before we start collecting data, we must finalize the data protection rules for T9. I've drafted the guidelines in A7, covering access control, data retention, and anonymization for reporting. The key principle is least-privilege access: frontline staff can only see feedback they own, while managers and BI can see aggregated, anonymized data.

I've reviewed A7. The rules are clear and align with our compliance standards, especially regarding the handling of personal data in insurance complaints. The 90-day retention period for raw feedback before anonymization is appropriate. I approve.

This is excellent work, @17689. Very thorough. This document is critical for the project's integrity. With @225681's review, are there any other questions or concerns about the data protection rules in A7?
It looks ok to me.

Hearing no objections, let's formally approve the data protection and access rules as documented in A7. (D8). This is a major milestone. I will now finalize the setup of the dashboard data source (A6) based on these rules.
Great. I'll ensure the access permissions on the shared feedback log (A5) reflect what we've documented in A7.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on next steps and roadmap.

messages.text: Hi all, the 4-week pilot run (T11) is now complete. A huge thank you for all your efforts in capturing and logging the feedback. I've analyzed the data and put together a preliminary evaluation report in A8. Please take some time to review it. The key takeaway is that the unified taxonomy has been a success, with our re-routing rate dropping to just 5% in the final week.

This is a great result. The data in A8 is very clear. The ability to distinguish between 'Claim Process' and 'Policy Wording' issues has already allowed us to identify a specific point of confusion in one of our policy documents. This process is already providing actionable insights. I strongly support scaling this.

From a technical perspective, the process was smooth. The manual routing was manageable for the pilot, but if we scale, we should investigate automating the tag-based ticket creation in our help desk system. The report in A8 provides a solid business case for that investment.
The report looks great! We got a lot of compliments about our new welcome call process. It's good to see that captured.
The paper checklist worked. We had no issues. The process did not disrupt the tours.

I'm glad to hear the positive feedback from all channels. It seems we have a consensus that the pilot was successful. The main question now is about our recommendation. Based on the results, I propose we recommend scaling the pilot into a permanent process, with the automation improvements @17689 suggested as a phase 2 objective. Does anyone disagree with this path?
I fully agree. We should move to scale.
Agree. The process is sound.
Yes, let's do it!

Fantastic. Then our decision is to recommend scaling the process. (D1). I will finalize the pilot evaluation report (T12) with this formal recommendation and the supporting data from A8. I'll share the final version by end of week for one last look before it goes to the stakeholders.
